blocks.text: The algorithm does not restart a search for every pair of indices. It carries a frequency map from one right endpoint to the next, adding the entering character and removing characters that leave from the left. That reuse is the running-window mechanism: candidates ending at successive right positions share almost all of their contents. The at-most-K predicate is also repairable by shrinking because removing characters cannot introduce a new distinct character. A global pair search would compare isolated endpoint relations rather than maintain the membership state of every character inside the range.

blocks.text: Both families can use same-direction pointers, and either may carry auxiliary state. What matters is the justification for not reconsidering candidates. In pair search, an endpoint relation—often supported by ordering—rules out a set of pairs. In a running window, the algorithm reuses state for contiguous candidates and advances left because earlier starts are invalid or dominated under the window rule. This proof-level distinction transfers to unfamiliar code more reliably than surface rules about direction, sorting, or the number of variables.
